question.text: Under Section 12 of the Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Act (WMDA), which of the following describes the position on liability for mere carriage of WMD-related materials without knowledge?

answer.text: Mere carriage or provision of services without knowledge by a public or private carrier of goods, courier, telecom service provider, postal service provider, or financial service provider is not an offence
All carriers are liable regardless of whether they had knowledge of the materials being transported
Only government-operated carriers are exempt from liability for carriage of such materials
The exemption applies exclusively to postal services and does not extend to financial service providers or couriers

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes Section 12 of the WMDA as providing that mere carriage of goods or provision of services without knowledge — including by a public or private carrier of goods, courier, telecommunication service provider, postal service provider, or financial service provider — is not an offence. The "without knowledge" condition is what triggers the relief. The Trap: The other options either impose strict liability regardless of knowledge, narrow the relief to a single class of carrier (postal or government), or drop categories that the workbook expressly lists. Note: The carrier list in the workbook expressly includes public or private carriers of goods alongside couriers, telecom, postal, and financial service providers. Do not narrow the list further than the source.
